name: Korean exfoliating mitt

lead: The Korean exfoliating mitt (often called an Italy towel or kessa-style mitt) is a rough viscose or nylon glove used on the whole body after soaking in warm water or a bath house. It rubs off visible rolls of loosened dead skin and is a staple of Korean bathing culture.
In looksmaxxing it is used for smoother, more even body skin and a short-term glow. The dead-skin removal is real and immediately visible, but the effect fades within days as the surface renews.

paras: Warm water softens and swells the stratum corneum, and friction then sheds the outer layers. A small study of this practice found that one scrubbing session temporarily lowered water-holding capacity, which recovered within a few days, while repeated scrubbing shortened stratum corneum turnover time without a measurable change in barrier function.

The evidence base is small, and mechanical rubbing is known to disturb the barrier. Over-scrubbing can cause redness, micro-tears, irritation and post-inflammatory darkening, particularly on darker skin and on inflamed or acne-prone areas. Sensible use is gentle, infrequent and followed by moisturiser. The satisfying amount of grey rolled skin is mostly dead skin and soap residue, not toxins.
